download-and-verify-a-release.text: You have cloned nothing. You want to know that a Singular release is what it says it is before you run it: that the files you downloaded are the files that were published, that the release names the formal model its evidence was checked against, and that the singular and open-datum commands built from it actually run a registry from creation to termination. One command answers all three, from the downloaded bytes alone, and either passes or refuses by name.

what-you-run.text: You need Nix with flakes enabled. Nothing else: no checkout, no credentials, no running node.

Name the release you are checking twice: once to choose the verifier that release ships, once as the release to download. The verifier downloads the release's three published assets from its GitHub release page without logging in:

The archive is unpacked into a fresh temporary directory, never inside a checkout. Pass --work DIR to choose that directory and keep what it leaves behind: the downloaded assets, the extracted archive and the receipts of every command the journey ran.

what-it-checks-in-order.text: Each check runs only when the ones before it passed, and the first one that fails ends the run with one line naming why.

The model revision is the commit of the application model, the formal specification the conformance evidence reads its statements at. The release states it in the archive as MODEL-REVISION; the verifier compares it with the revision the conformance evidence of the same release is compiled against. The journey is the one on the archive's run page: a registry is created, a key inserted, its payload updated and the key terminated, each a separate singular or open-datum process on one development network the verifier starts and stops itself, with an inspect after every write.

Before starting the journey, the verifier strips and inspects the actual compiled singular and open-datum executables and reads their resolved registry CLI build flags. Both must exclude hidden test inputs and disable the test flag. It then records every ordinary journey invocation: all five commands must run without hidden harness inputs, and no hold marker may appear.

Fault injection, crash recovery, race controls and independent trie-capability observations run in the explicit test build. Their unchanged assertions are separate required CI evidence. They do not claim to have run inside these extracted release binaries.

what-a-refusal-means.text: A refusal is one line, verify-release: REFUSED <name>: <detail>, and the exit status is 1.
A release that passes prints its tag, both archive checksums, the model revision and the directory it was verified in.

checking-files-you-already-have.text: If you downloaded the three assets yourself, point the verifier at their directory; every check after the download is the same:
From v0.8.0 on, every release is verified this way by the release workflow itself, right after it is published.
